title: Tokens misdirected to DssBlow2 are unrecoverable and do not discharge an obligation owed to Sky
content:
A.4.6.1.1.1.1.1.1 is unusually blunt: "Only Dai or USDS are supported by DssBlow2. Any other tokens sent to DssBlow2 are not recoverable by Sky. Senders bear full responsibility; such transfers are not considered a valid receipt of funds owed."

The first half is a technical fact — the contract has no rescue function, so anything it cannot process is stranded permanently, and not even governance can retrieve it. The second half is the load-bearing part, and it is a claim about obligations rather than about code. A payer who sends the wrong asset to the right address has not paid. They still owe the money, and they have also lost the tokens.

Stating this in the ruleset closes a dispute that would otherwise be genuinely arguable. A debtor could reasonably contend they performed by sending value to Sky's published address and that the loss is a shared misfortune, or that the protocol should be estopped from claiming twice. Pre-declaring where the risk of misdirection sits removes the argument and, more importantly, aligns incentives: the party choosing what to send bears the consequence of getting it wrong, which is the only party able to prevent the error.

The broader pattern for on-chain systems: irreversibility means payment instructions are safety-critical documentation, and the accompanying rule must say what happens when they are not followed. Sky chooses documented strictness over a recovery mechanism — no admin escape hatch on the contract, and no forgiveness of the underlying debt.
description: The Atlas states that non-Dai/USDS sent to the contract is lost, senders bear full responsibility, and such a transfer is "not considered a valid receipt of funds owed" — the debt survives the loss.
